questions.q: What do resources inside the same resource group share?
options: The exact same physical server
A lifecycle - they're typically deployed, managed, and deleted together
Identical virtual machine sizes
A single shared IP address
questions.explain: A resource group is defined by shared lifecycle: resources inside it are managed and deleted as a unit, with no separate step to empty it first.

questions.q: When you run az group create --location eastus, what does that location actually control?
options: Where the resource group's own metadata is stored - resources inside can still be deployed to other regions
The region where Microsoft Entra authenticates users
The billing region used on the invoice
Every resource created inside that group must also be in East US
questions.explain: A resource group's location only stores its metadata; individual resources inside it can be deployed to any region.

options: A monitoring dashboard for resource costs only
A legacy system replaced entirely by Bicep
The single management layer that every deployment tool - Portal, CLI, PowerShell, templates - calls underneath
A separate product you must install alongside Azure CLI
questions.explain: Every Azure management tool, regardless of interface, sends its requests to the same ARM API, which is why RBAC and policy apply consistently no matter which tool is used.

questions.q: Why is an ARM template considered idempotent?
options: It automatically deletes resources it previously created
It requires a new resource group every time it runs
It can only be submitted exactly once per subscription
Re-submitting the same template only changes what's actually different from what's already deployed
questions.explain: ARM compares a submitted template against the current state and only applies the differences, making it safe to re-run the same template repeatedly.

questions.q: What does a CanNotDelete resource lock do?
options: Automatically backs up every resource nightly
Prevents any user from viewing the resource group
Only applies to resources created through the Portal, not the CLI
Blocks deletion of the resource group or resource until the lock is removed, regardless of a user's RBAC permissions
questions.explain: A CanNotDelete lock is an extra layer of protection against accidental deletion, independent of whatever delete permissions a user's RBAC role grants them.
